derived.prompt: Is 10 times the square root of 2 a rational number?

chain: The square root of 2 is a rational number. (edit)
Multiplying a rational number by 10 gives a rational number. (class rule of the rationals)
So 10 times the square root of 2 is a rational number: yes.

The square root of 2 is an irrational nu.why: One of the most often stated facts of mathematics, the textbook example of an irrational number, with a proof every course repeats. Thousands of exact mentions in Dolma across its spellings. It is provable, but a model meets it as a stated fact far more often than it could work it out.

sources.quote: Pythagoreans discovered that the diagonal of a square is incommensurable with its side, or in modern language, that the square root of two is irrational.

sources.query: square root of two is irrational
the square root of 2 is an irrational number

sources.note: most sampled hits are proofs by contradiction ("suppose the square root of 2 is rational")

1 divided by the square root of 2 is not.why: 1/√2 is written often as a value (the sine of 45 degrees, about 0.707), but its rationality is seldom the point: texts make the irrationality claim about the square root of 2 itself. A model works it out from that and the rule that the reciprocal of a rational is rational. The direct forms have a handful of hits against over a thousand for the premise.

Twice the sine of 45 degrees is not a ra.why: People write that sin 45° is √2/2 (in trigonometry tables) and that √2 is irrational (in number theory), in different texts for different purposes; doubling the sine of 45 degrees and asking whether the result is rational is not something anyone writes. A model must first recognise the value as the square root of 2. The exact forms are absent.

The reciprocal of a nonzero rational num.why: The reciprocal of p/q (p, q nonzero) is q/p, again a fraction of two integers.

The square root of 2 is greater than 1..why: The square root of 2 is about 1.4142, as the first sentence of its Wikipedia article says.

sources.quote: The square root of 2 (approximately 1.4142) is the positive real number that, when multiplied by itself or squared, equals the number 2.

10 times the square root of 2 is not a r.why: People state that the square root of 2 is irrational, and that multiplying rationals gives a rational; nobody has a reason to state the rationality of 10 times the square root of 2 in particular, an arbitrary multiple that is no named constant and no textbook exercise. A model works it out from the two general facts. The exact forms are absent, while the expression itself and both premises are common.

Multiplying a rational number by 10 give.why: 10 = 10/1, and the product of two fractions of integers is again a fraction of integers: (p/q) × 10 = 10p/q.

Twice the sine of 45 degrees is the squa.why: sin 45° = √2/2 = 1/√2 is a standard value in every trigonometry table, including Wikipedia's; twice it is √2.

sources.quote: 9 is the fourth composite number, the first odd composite number, a square, a Motzkin number, and the number of derangements of 4 items.

7 plus the square root of 2 is not a rat.why: 7 plus the square root of 2 is an arbitrary sum that names no constant (1 plus the square root of 2 would be the silver ratio, which is why 7 is used): people state that the square root of 2 is irrational and, separately, that sums of rationals are rational, but nobody writes the rationality of this particular sum. A model works it out by adding 7. The exact forms are absent while both premises are common.

Adding 7 to a rational number gives a ra.why: The sum of two rational numbers is rational, and 7 is rational.

notes: Stored edit (very_unlikely): the irrationality of the square root of 2 is stated thousands of times. Mathematics leaves out worlds and the indeterminate query (README, Shape per topic): a fact about a number, a shape or a proof rests on definitions, so the edit leaves no consistent world to split between; the record has 4 determinate derived queries. Derived queries ask what the edit forces with the definitions held fixed; a model that still gives the old answer holds the edit only as a patch. The relation is has_rationality (functional: a real number is rational or irrational, not both). The near query asks the old class ("Is the square root of 2 an irrational number?"). Because the relation has two values this is the negation of the edit; it is kept as the functional near query because no other one-hop form of this fact is stored often enough to be counted ("cannot be written as a fraction" is under 100 exact mentions), and the topic needs a functional near query. The far query is stored and binding: the diagonal of a square with sides of length 1 reaches the square root of 2 by a description the model holds separately. That the diagonal is incommensurable with the side (Hippasus) is famous, but it is the same fact as the irrationality of the square root of 2 and the edit overturns it, so it is stored evidence that must move, not a route around the edit. Three derived queries are inheritance: the edit makes the square root of 2 a member of the class rational, and a class rule of the rationals then applies to a new number (times 10, plus 7, reciprocal); they are task answer, logic fol, theory arithmetic. The fourth is binding: it reaches the square root of 2 by twice the sine of 45 degrees, a description the model holds separately. The continued-fraction bridge (missed by 3 models) and 3-hop queries are gone. 1 plus the square root of 2 (the silver ratio, whose irrationality is stated in its own right) became 7 plus the square root of 2. Negation is worded "Is it true that X is not Y?" (CRITERIA Rule 6).
